subject: Next steps: ranker prototype setup & evaluation asks
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Palmer <alex@searchly.com>, Priya Singh <p.singh@searchly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up + concrete asks from today’s ranker call

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and some concrete engineering questions so we can stand up a focused PoC: 

Call recap (short):
- Goal: integrate Redwood ranking pipeline to improve Searchly product relevance for commerce queries (reduce false positives, boost intent matches).
- Scope for PoC: integrate our retrieval -> rerank flow on a 5k sample of queries, measure NDCG@10 / MRR, and evaluate latency impact.

Engineering asks we need answers to before the PoC:
1) SDK & languages — which runtime will your infra use for the initial integration (Node, Python, Go)? we’ll provide short SDK snippets.
2) Auth model — will you prefer a long-lived API key, short-lived service account tokens, or OAuth delegation from your app? any security requirements (IP allowlists / private VPC)?
3) Routing & topology — do you plan to do initial retrieval in your service and call Redwood for rerank only (preferred), or call Redwood for both retrieval + rerank?
4) Reranker integration pattern — do you want a pure reordering of top-N candidates or a scoring-based approach where we return scores for all candidates? recommended default: retrieve top-100 -> rerank -> return top-10.
5) Structured/tooling — do you need structured output or tool-calling from the model for downstream actions (e.g., category tags, fulfillment hooks)?
6) Evaluation data — can you share a representative sample (CSV of queries + golden URL ids); we need ID mapping to compute NDCG/MRR. I attached sample-queries.csv as an example format.

Next steps I propose:
- You reply with answers to the six items above and attach a 5k sample;
- We create an ephemeral API key and a sandbox dataset for you to call (PoC environ);
- Run baseline retrieval metrics (your current system) and compare vs. Redwood rerank;
- We’ll provide a short evaluation script (python) to compute NDCG@K/MRR/Recall@K and a perf budget.

I attached a short integration guide and a sample queries CSV to illustrate expected fields. If that’s fine I’ll loop in Aditya to prepare the SDK snippets and a recommended config (batching, top_k defaults, latency targets).

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-integration-guide.pdf (stub)
From: Alex Palmer <alex@searchly.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <p.singh@searchly.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + concrete asks from today’s ranker call

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers below: 
- Runtime: backend search service is Node (Express) for the PoC; we also have a Python analytics job.
- Auth: security team prefers short-lived service account tokens, but we can accept an API key for sandbox traffic. IP allowlists are possible.
- Routing: we currently run retrieval in our service (BM25 + dense retriever). Plan is to call Redwood only for rerank (reordering top-N).
- Rerank approach: we prefer reordering top-N (score + explanation fields are helpful).
- Structured output: yes — category tags (taxonomy id) would be very helpful; no tool-calls required for PoC.
- Data: I can share a 5k sample — requested format looks fine.

Two questions for you:
1) For the evaluation script you mentioned — will it support NDCG@5/10, MRR, and pairwise win rates?
2) What are your recommended defaults for top_N retrieval (to feed the reranker) and top_k output? We’d like to start conservative to avoid latency spikes.

I’ll upload the sample and loop Priya for sec.

—Alex
Alex Palmer
Head of Search — Searchly
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Palmer <alex@searchly.com>, Priya Singh <p.singh@searchly.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + concrete asks from today’s ranker call

Hi Alex / team —

Short technical replies and defaults we recommend for a Node-based PoC: 
- SDKs: official SDKs for Node + Python + Go. For Node we have an express middleware snippet that turns a request with candidate ids into a rerank call (I’ll paste below).
- Auth: we'll provision an ephemeral service-account token that rotates (recommended). Sandbox API key is OK for initial testing. If you need IP allowlist, tell us the CIDRs.
- Recommended pattern: retrieval on your side -> Redwood rerank(top_N=100) -> return top_k=10. This balances recall and compute; top_N=50 is acceptable for smaller latency budgets.
- Latency: expect ~12–40ms per item for large transformer-based rerankers on single request; with batching and our continuous batching runtime you should see amortized token latency under 120ms for a typical request when reranking 100 candidates. We’ll provide perf profiles for the exact model variant.
- Structured output: we support returning a JSON field with taxonomy ids and confidence scores. If you need deterministic category labels, we recommend an additional lightweight classifier step cached in Redis.

Sample Node snippet (conceptual):

// pseudo-code
// const candidates = [ {id: 'u123', text: '...'}, ... ];
// const resp = await redwood.rerank({model: 'rerank-v2', candidates, top_k: 10, return_scores: true});
// resp.items -> ordered list with scores and optional structured tags

Related links:
- internal playbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/infra/ranker-playbook
- SDK quickstart: https://drive.redwood.ai/sdk/node-quickstart

I’ll prepare the exact config (model id, quantization, batching window) after we see the sample queries and desired latency SLA. Happy to jump on a quick architecture call if you want to discuss caching/kv-store for candidate retrieval.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Palmer <alex@searchly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <p.singh@searchly.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + concrete asks from today’s ranker call

Thanks Aditya — super helpful. A couple more specific evaluation asks from our analytics lead: 
- Yes, include NDCG@5, NDCG@10, MRR, and pairwise win-rate. We’d also like Recall@100 and a simple latency-percentile table (p50/p90/p99) aggregated by query length.
- For labeling, we have a graded relevance score (0–3). Will your evaluation script accept graded relevance or do you prefer binary?
- On top_k defaults: we’ll start with retrieval top_N=100 -> rerank -> output top_k=10. Can you share a recommended per-request token and batch size to hit p95 < 250ms?

We’ll upload the 5k sample later today.

—Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Palmer <alex@searchly.com>, Priya Singh <p.singh@searchly.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + concrete asks from today’s ranker call

Alex / team —

Thanks — we can support graded relevance (0–3) in the evaluation script; NDCG handles graded labels directly. We’ll include NDCG@5/10, MRR, pairwise win-rate, Recall@100, and latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99).

For the PoC timeline and next steps: 
- Today: you upload 5k CSV (format: query_id, query_text, candidate_ids[], gold_candidate_id, grade).
- +1 business day: Redwood provides sandbox credentials (ephemeral token) and an example evaluation repo (python) that runs metrics and a perf harness.
- +3 business days: run baseline vs. rerank on your infra and share results.

We’ll aim for a p95 < 250ms recommendation by default with the following starting config: model=rerank-v2-llm-small, retrieval top_N=100, server-side batching window=15ms, recommended batch size=16–64 depending on load. We’ll provide tuning knobs after initial runs.

I’ve granted an ephemeral sandbox token that will be valid for 72 hours and uploaded the integration guide in the sandbox drive folder. Please confirm when you upload the 5k sample and we’ll push the SDK snippets and the evaluation script.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
